statusbar.group.machine.note: A group's heading in the palette of the Preferences' status bar editor (Preferences): the elements that can be added, by what they show.

statusbar.group.cpu.note: A group's heading in the palette of the Preferences' status bar editor (Preferences): the elements that can be added, by what they show.

statusbar.group.network.note: A group's heading in the palette of the Preferences' status bar editor (Preferences): the elements that can be added, by what they show.

statusbar.group.disks.note: A group's heading in the palette of the Preferences' status bar editor (Preferences): the elements that can be added, by what they show.

statusbar.group.usb.note: A group's heading in the palette of the Preferences' status bar editor (Preferences): the elements that can be added, by what they show.

statusbar.group.graphics.note: A group's heading in the palette of the Preferences' status bar editor (Preferences): the elements that can be added, by what they show.

statusbar.group.input.note: A group's heading in the palette of the Preferences' status bar editor (Preferences): the elements that can be added, by what they show.

statusbar.group.layout.note: A group's heading in the palette of the Preferences' status bar editor (Preferences): the elements that can be added, by what they show.

statusbar.kind.state.note: The name of a status bar element (the state kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.state.about.message: Whether the machine is powered off, booting, or running, and what this emulator is doing.
statusbar.kind.state.about.note: What the Power state status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.vcpus.note: The name of a status bar element (the vcpus kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.vcpus.about.message: How many vCPUs the machine has.
statusbar.kind.vcpus.about.note: What the vCPUs status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.ram.note: The name of a status bar element (the ram kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.ram.about.note: What the RAM status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.uptime.note: The name of a status bar element (the uptime kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.uptime.about.message: How long the machine has been running.
statusbar.kind.uptime.about.note: What the Uptime status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.clock.note: The name of a status bar element (the clock kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.clock.about.note: What the Clock status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.memory.note: The name of a status bar element (the memory kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.memory.about.message: How much memory the machine's tab uses, as this emulator counts it.
statusbar.kind.memory.about.note: What the Tab memory status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.mips.note: The name of a status bar element (the mips kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider. Per-device elements wrap it ("{{name}}, each vCPU").

statusbar.kind.mips.about.message: Millions of guest instructions run a second.
statusbar.kind.mips.about.note: What the MIPS status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.jit.note: The name of a status bar element (the jit kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider. Per-device elements wrap it ("{{name}}, each vCPU").

statusbar.kind.jit.about.message: The share of instructions run as compiled code; the rest are interpreted.
statusbar.kind.jit.about.note: What the JIT share status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.irqs.note: The name of a status bar element (the irqs kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.irqs.about.note: What the IRQ/s status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.blocks.note: The name of a status bar element (the blocks kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.blocks.about.message: Blocks the JIT has compiled since boot, and how often its cache was flushed.
statusbar.kind.blocks.about.note: What the Blocks compiled status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.compile.note: The name of a status bar element (the compile kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.compile.about.message: Time spent compiling since boot, on all vCPUs.
statusbar.kind.compile.about.note: What the Compile time status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.jitcache.note: The name of a status bar element (the jitcache kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.jitcache.about.message: How much of the JIT's cache its compiled code fills.
statusbar.kind.jitcache.about.note: What the JIT cache status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.netrate.note: The name of a status bar element (the netrate kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider. Per-device elements wrap it ("{{name}}, each vCPU").

statusbar.kind.netrate.about.message: Bytes a second received and sent by the machine.
statusbar.kind.netrate.about.note: What the Network traffic status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.nettotal.note: The name of a status bar element (the nettotal kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider. Per-device elements wrap it ("{{name}}, each vCPU").

statusbar.kind.nettotal.about.message: Bytes received and sent since the machine started.
statusbar.kind.nettotal.about.note: What the Network total status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.link.note: The name of a status bar element (the link kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider. Per-device elements wrap it ("{{name}}, each vCPU").

statusbar.kind.link.about.message: The state of an adapter's connection: connected, connecting, waiting for a login, or off.
statusbar.kind.link.about.note: What the Connection status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.diskrate.note: The name of a status bar element (the diskrate kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider. Per-device elements wrap it ("{{name}}, each vCPU").

statusbar.kind.diskrate.about.message: Bytes a second read (R) and written (W).
statusbar.kind.diskrate.about.note: What the Disk speed status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.disktotal.note: The name of a status bar element (the disktotal kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider. Per-device elements wrap it ("{{name}}, each vCPU").

statusbar.kind.disktotal.about.message: Bytes read (R) and written (W) since the machine started.
statusbar.kind.disktotal.about.note: What the Disk total status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.usbrate.note: The name of a status bar element (the usbrate kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.usbrate.about.message: Bytes a second the machine's USB devices sent it (in) and took from it (out), all of them together.
statusbar.kind.usbrate.about.note: What the USB traffic status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips. In and out are as the guest sees them: in is what a device gave the guest.

statusbar.kind.usbtotal.note: The name of a status bar element (the usbtotal kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.usbtotal.about.message: Bytes the machine's USB devices sent it (in) and took from it (out) since it started.
statusbar.kind.usbtotal.about.note: What the USB total status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.gpu.note: The name of a status bar element (the gpu kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.gpu.about.message: How the screen is drawn: 3D through WebGL2 (virgl), or 2D. It turns amber when this browser renders in software.
statusbar.kind.gpu.about.note: What the Renderer status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.fps.note: The name of a status bar element (the fps kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.fps.about.note: What the Frame rate status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.video.note: The name of a status bar element (the video kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.video.about.message: The video streams the guest decodes through this browser (VA-API over virgl, on 3D machines), with their codecs and pictures a second.
statusbar.kind.video.about.note: What the Video decode status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.vulkan.note: The name of a status bar element (the vulkan kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.vulkan.about.message: The guest's programs using Vulkan (through Venus, on this browser's WebGPU), with their submits a second. Shown on machines with Vulkan.
statusbar.kind.vulkan.about.note: What the Vulkan activity status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.pointer.note: The name of a status bar element (the pointer kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.pointer.about.message: Whether the screen holds the mouse (green), will take it on a click (grey), or the mouse lock is off (dim).
statusbar.kind.pointer.about.note: What the Mouse lock status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.keyboard.note: The name of a status bar element (the keyboard kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.keyboard.about.message: Where typing goes: to the machine (green), or nowhere until you click the screen. In full screen with the keyboard lock, the browser's shortcuts go to the machine too.
statusbar.kind.keyboard.about.note: What the Keyboard status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.mic.note: The name of a status bar element (the mic kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.mic.about.message: Shown while the machine records from the microphone, or when this browser refused it the microphone.
statusbar.kind.mic.about.note: What the Microphone status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.spacer.note: The name of a status bar element (the spacer kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.spacer.about.message: Takes up the free space, pushing what follows to the right.
statusbar.kind.spacer.about.note: What the Spacer status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.kind.divider.note: The name of a status bar element (the divider kind) in the Preferences' status bar editor: on its chip in the palette, over its settings, in tooltips; in the bar itself, the tooltip of a spacer or divider.

statusbar.kind.divider.about.note: What the Divider status bar element shows: in the Preferences' status bar editor, under the element's name when it's chosen and in its chips' tooltips.

statusbar.name.each.cpu.note: The name, in the Preferences' status bar editor and its tooltips, of a per-device status bar element that shows each vCPU in turn. {{name}} is the element's name (MIPS, Network traffic…).

statusbar.name.each.net.note: The name, in the Preferences' status bar editor and its tooltips, of a per-device status bar element that shows each adapter in turn. {{name}} is the element's name (MIPS, Network traffic…).

statusbar.name.each.disk.note: The name, in the Preferences' status bar editor and its tooltips, of a per-device status bar element that shows each disk in turn. {{name}} is the element's name (MIPS, Network traffic…).

statusbar.name.any.cpu.note: The name of a palette chip in the Preferences' status bar editor that adds a status bar element for a single vCPU (its number is chosen after). {{name}} is the element's name.

statusbar.name.any.net.note: The name of a palette chip in the Preferences' status bar editor that adds a status bar element for a single adapter (its number is chosen after). {{name}} is the element's name.

statusbar.name.any.disk.note: The name of a palette chip in the Preferences' status bar editor that adds a status bar element for a single disk (its number is chosen after). {{name}} is the element's name.

statusbar.name.one.cpu.note: The name, in the Preferences' status bar editor and its tooltips, of a status bar element for one vCPU. {{name}} is the element's name, {{index}} the vCPU's number (from 0, as the guest names them).

statusbar.name.one.net.note: The name, in the Preferences' status bar editor and its tooltips, of a status bar element for one adapter. {{name}} is the element's name, {{index}} the adapter's number (from 1, as the machine's tabs list them).

statusbar.name.one.disk.note: The name, in the Preferences' status bar editor and its tooltips, of a status bar element for one disk. {{name}} is the element's name, {{index}} the disk's number (from 1, as the machine's tabs list them).

statusbar.link.connected.note: The Connection element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text when drawn as an icon), when the adapter is connected. {{name}} is the adapter's name (Adapter 1…).

statusbar.link.connecting.note: The Connection element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text when drawn as an icon), when the adapter is connecting. {{name}} is the adapter's name (Adapter 1…).

statusbar.link.login.note: The Connection element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text when drawn as an icon), when the adapter waits for the user to log in. {{name}} is the adapter's name (Adapter 1…).

statusbar.link.error.note: The Connection element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text when drawn as an icon), when the adapter failed to connect. {{name}} is the adapter's name (Adapter 1…).

statusbar.link.off.note: The Connection element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text when drawn as an icon), when the adapter has no connection, or it's stopped. {{name}} is the adapter's name (Adapter 1…).

statusbar.adapter.note: A network adapter's name in the status bar (the page's footer) (Connection and network traffic elements) and their tooltips. {{number}} counts from 1, as the machine's Network tab lists them.

statusbar.state.title.note: Tooltip of the power state at the left of the status bar (the page's footer). {{state}} is the state's words (Running, Powered off, Loading 40%…).

statusbar.clock.title.note: Tooltip of the Clock element in the status bar (the page's footer). {{time}} is your computer's time of day, as the browser's locale writes it.

statusbar.pointer.held.note: The Mouse lock element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text when drawn as an icon) while the screen holds the mouse.

statusbar.pointer.held.title.message: The screen holds the mouse. Press Esc to release it.
statusbar.pointer.held.title.note: Tooltip of the Mouse lock element in the status bar (the page's footer) while the screen holds the mouse.

statusbar.pointer.on.note: The Mouse lock element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text) while the lock is on and a click on the screen would take the mouse.

statusbar.pointer.on.title.message: A click on the screen will lock the mouse to it.
statusbar.pointer.on.title.note: Tooltip of the Mouse lock element in the status bar (the page's footer) while the lock is on but the screen doesn't hold the mouse.

statusbar.pointer.off.note: The Mouse lock element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text) while the toolbar's mouse lock is off.

statusbar.pointer.off.title.message: The mouse lock is off. Turn it on from the toolbar's Mouse lock menu.
statusbar.pointer.off.title.note: Tooltip of the Mouse lock element in the status bar (the page's footer) while the lock is off.

statusbar.keyboard.locked.note: The Keyboard element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text) in full screen with the keyboard lock: every key goes to the machine.

statusbar.keyboard.locked.title.message: Keys and the browser's shortcuts go to the machine, in full screen with the keyboard lock. Hold Esc to leave full screen.
statusbar.keyboard.locked.title.note: Tooltip of the Keyboard element in the status bar (the page's footer) in full screen with the keyboard lock.

statusbar.keyboard.typing.note: The Keyboard element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text) while the screen or the terminal has the focus.

statusbar.keyboard.typing.title.message: Keys go to the machine. This browser keeps its own shortcuts; full screen sends them to the machine too.
statusbar.keyboard.typing.title.note: Tooltip of the Keyboard element in the status bar (the page's footer) while keys go to the machine.

statusbar.keyboard.click.note: The Keyboard element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text) while keys don't go to the machine.

statusbar.keyboard.click.title.message: Keys don't go to the machine. Click the screen to type to it.
statusbar.keyboard.click.title.note: Tooltip of the Keyboard element in the status bar (the page's footer) while keys don't go to the machine.

statusbar.mic.on.note: The Microphone element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text) while the machine records from the microphone.

statusbar.mic.on.title.message: The machine is recording from the microphone.
statusbar.mic.on.title.note: Tooltip of the Microphone element in the status bar (the page's footer) while the machine records.

statusbar.mic.denied.note: The Microphone element in the status bar (the page's footer) (or its screen-reader text) when the machine records but the browser refused the microphone.

statusbar.mic.denied.title.message: The machine is recording, but this browser refused it the microphone, so it gets silence.
statusbar.mic.denied.title.note: Tooltip of the Microphone element in the status bar (the page's footer) when the browser refused the microphone.

statusbar.link.other.note: The Connection element in the status bar (the page's footer) for a connection phase the page has no words for (another version's). {{name}} is the adapter's name, {{phase}} the phase's code.

statusbar.link.title.note: Tooltip of the Connection element in the status bar (the page's footer). {{name}} is the adapter's name, {{text}} its connection and how it's going (as the Network menu says it).

statusbar.gpu.renderer.vendor.note: The last line of the Renderer element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): the browser's WebGL2 renderer {{renderer}} and its vendor {{vendor}}, as the browser names them.

statusbar.gpu.renderer.note: The last line of the Renderer element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer) when the browser names no vendor: {{renderer}} is the WebGL2 renderer, as the browser names it.

statusbar.gpu.canvas.note: The Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer) when a 2D machine's screen is drawn on a 2D canvas (no hardware WebGL2 in this browser).

statusbar.gpu.2d.note: The Renderer element's short value (next to its icon, when drawn as an icon) in the status bar (the page's footer): the screen is 2D.

statusbar.gpu.canvas.title.message: The screen is 2D, drawn on a canvas, because this browser has no hardware WebGL2.
statusbar.gpu.canvas.title.note: Tooltip of the Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer) when the screen is drawn on a 2D canvas.

statusbar.gpu.framebuffer.note: The Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer) on a machine whose screen is its simple framebuffer (no virtio-gpu: the address's display=simple), drawn on a 2D canvas.

statusbar.gpu.framebuffer.title.message: The screen is the machine's simple framebuffer, drawn on a canvas: it has no graphics device.
statusbar.gpu.framebuffer.title.note: Tooltip of the Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer) on a machine whose screen is its simple framebuffer.

statusbar.gpu.3d.note: The Renderer element's short value (next to its icon) in the status bar (the page's footer): the screen is 3D (virgl).

statusbar.gpu.software.3d.note: The Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer) when a 3D machine's WebGL2 is rendered in software by the browser (slow; drawn amber).

statusbar.gpu.software.2d.note: The Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer) when a 2D machine's WebGL2 is rendered in software by the browser.

statusbar.gpu.software.3d.title.message: The screen is 3D through WebGL2, which this browser renders in software, so it is slow.
statusbar.gpu.software.3d.title.note: Tooltip of the Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer), 3D in software (the renderer's name may follow on a line of its own).

statusbar.gpu.software.2d.title.message: The screen is 2D through WebGL2, which this browser renders in software, so it is slow.
statusbar.gpu.software.2d.title.note: Tooltip of the Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer), 2D in software (the renderer's name may follow on a line of its own).

statusbar.gpu.webgl2.3d.note: The Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer) when a 3D machine draws through WebGL2 on the GPU.

statusbar.gpu.webgl2.2d.note: The Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer) when a 2D machine's screen is drawn through WebGL2 on the GPU.

statusbar.gpu.webgl2.3d.title.message: The screen is 3D (virgl), drawn through WebGL2 on the GPU.
statusbar.gpu.webgl2.3d.title.note: Tooltip of the Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer), 3D on the GPU (the renderer's name may follow on a line of its own).

statusbar.gpu.webgl2.2d.title.message: The screen is 2D, drawn through WebGL2 on the GPU.
statusbar.gpu.webgl2.2d.title.note: Tooltip of the Renderer element in the status bar (the page's footer), 2D on the GPU (the renderer's name may follow on a line of its own).

statusbar.fps.note: The Frame rate element in the status bar (the page's footer). {{fps}} is the screen updates drawn in the last second.

statusbar.fps.title.note: Tooltip of the Frame rate element in the status bar (the page's footer). {{fps}} is the screen updates drawn in the last second.

statusbar.video.idle.note: The Video decode element in the status bar (the page's footer) while the guest decodes no video through VA-API.

statusbar.video.idle.title.message: The guest isn't decoding any video through VA-API now.
statusbar.video.idle.title.note: Tooltip of the Video decode element in the status bar (the page's footer) while no stream is decoded.

statusbar.video.hw.note: The Video decode element in the status bar (the page's footer) before its first second's count: {{codecs}} are the streams' codecs (H.264 High…), comma-separated; hw says every open decoder asked for hardware.

statusbar.video.hw.fps.note: The Video decode element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{codecs}} are the streams' codecs, comma-separated; hw is short for hardware decoding; {{fps}} the pictures decoded in the last second.

statusbar.video.sw.note: The Video decode element in the status bar (the page's footer) before its first second's count: {{codecs}} are the streams' codecs (H.264 High…), comma-separated; sw says every open decoder asked for software (or not all of them asked for hardware).

statusbar.video.sw.fps.note: The Video decode element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{codecs}} are the streams' codecs, comma-separated; sw is short for software decoding; {{fps}} the pictures decoded in the last second.

statusbar.video.short.note: The Video decode element's short value (next to its icon) in the status bar (the page's footer): {{streams}} is the number of video streams, {{fps}} the pictures decoded in the last second.

statusbar.video.stream.hardware.note: In a stream's line of the Video decode element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): its decoder asked for hardware decoding.

statusbar.video.stream.software.note: In a stream's line of the Video decode element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): its decoder decodes in software.

statusbar.video.stream.closed.note: In a stream's line of the Video decode element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): the stream has no open decoder.

statusbar.video.stream.fps.note: In a stream's line of the Video decode element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): {{fps}} is the stream's pictures decoded in the last second.

statusbar.video.stream.note: A stream's line in the Video decode element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): {{profile}} its codec, {{width}}×{{height}} its picture size, {{facts}} what's known of its decoder (hardware or software, no decoder now, N pictures a second), comma-separated.

statusbar.video.title.message: Video decode. A stream marked hardware asked for a hardware decoder; this browser doesn't say whether it got one.
statusbar.video.title.note: First line of the Video decode element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer); a line per stream follows.

statusbar.video.errors.note: Last line of the Video decode element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer), when the browser's decoders failed: {{errors}} is how many times.

statusbar.vulkan.none.note: The Vulkan element in the status bar (the page's footer) when the browser gave the machine no WebGPU device: the guest's Vulkan programs draw nothing.

statusbar.vulkan.none.title.message: This browser gave the machine no WebGPU device: the guest's Vulkan programs run but draw nothing.
statusbar.vulkan.none.title.note: Tooltip of the Vulkan element in the status bar (the page's footer) when there is no WebGPU device.

statusbar.vulkan.idle.note: The Vulkan element in the status bar (the page's footer) while no guest program holds a Vulkan device.

statusbar.vulkan.idle.title.message: No program in the guest is using Vulkan now.
statusbar.vulkan.idle.title.note: First line of the Vulkan element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer) while no guest program holds a Vulkan device; the adapter's line may follow.

statusbar.vulkan.programs_one.note: The Vulkan element in the status bar (the page's footer) before its first second's count: {{count}} is the guest's programs using Vulkan now (Venus contexts).

statusbar.vulkan.programs_other.note: The Vulkan element in the status bar (the page's footer) before its first second's count: {{count}} is the guest's programs using Vulkan now (Venus contexts).

statusbar.vulkan.programs.rate_one.note: The Vulkan element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{count}} is the guest's programs using Vulkan now, {{submits}} the GPU submits it made in the last second.

statusbar.vulkan.programs.rate_other.note: The Vulkan element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{count}} is the guest's programs using Vulkan now, {{submits}} the GPU submits they made in the last second.

statusbar.vulkan.short.note: The Vulkan element's short value (next to its icon) in the status bar (the page's footer): {{count}} programs using Vulkan, {{submits}} GPU submits in the last second.

statusbar.vulkan.title_one.message: {{count}} program in the guest is using Vulkan (each Vulkan instance counts as one).
statusbar.vulkan.title_one.note: First line of the Vulkan element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): {{count}} is the guest's Venus contexts now.

statusbar.vulkan.title_other.message: {{count}} programs in the guest are using Vulkan (each Vulkan instance counts as one).
statusbar.vulkan.title_other.note: First line of the Vulkan element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): {{count}} is the guest's Venus contexts now.

statusbar.vulkan.rates.message: {{submits}} GPU submits and {{draws}} draws in the last second.
statusbar.vulkan.rates.note: A line of the Vulkan element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): what the guest's Vulkan programs sent to this browser's WebGPU in the last second.

statusbar.vulkan.adapter.message: Drawn on this browser's WebGPU adapter: {{adapter}}.
statusbar.vulkan.adapter.note: Last line of the Vulkan element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): {{adapter}} is the WebGPU adapter's vendor, architecture and description as the browser gives them.

statusbar.vulkan.adapter.software.message: Drawn on this browser's WebGPU adapter: {{adapter}}, which renders in software.
statusbar.vulkan.adapter.software.note: Last line of the Vulkan element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer) when the WebGPU adapter is a software one (SwiftShader, a fallback adapter): {{adapter}} is its vendor, architecture and description.

statusbar.vcpus_one.note: The vCPUs element in the status bar (the page's footer) and its tooltip: {{count}} is the running machine's number of virtual CPUs.

statusbar.vcpus_other.note: The vCPUs element in the status bar (the page's footer) and its tooltip: {{count}} is the running machine's number of virtual CPUs.

statusbar.ram.title.note: Tooltip of the RAM element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{mib}} is the machine's RAM in MiB.

statusbar.uptime.note: The Uptime element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{time}} is how long the machine has run, as hours:minutes:seconds.

statusbar.uptime.title.note: Tooltip of the Uptime element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{time}} is how long the machine has run, as hours:minutes:seconds.

statusbar.memory.note: The Tab memory element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{size}} is what the machine costs its browser tab (a size in MiB or GiB).

statusbar.memory.title.message: The tab uses about {{size}}, as this emulator counts it.
statusbar.memory.title.note: Tooltip of the Tab memory element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{size}} is the tab's memory (a size in MiB or GiB).

statusbar.irqs.note: The IRQ/s element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{irqs}} is the interrupts taken in the last second.

statusbar.irqs.title.note: Tooltip of the IRQ/s element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{irqs}} is the interrupts taken in the last second.

statusbar.blocks.flushed.note: The Blocks compiled element in the status bar (the page's footer) once the JIT's cache was flushed: {{blocks}} blocks compiled since boot, {{flushes}} how many times the cache was flushed.

statusbar.blocks.flushed.short.note: The Blocks compiled element's short value (next to its icon) in the status bar (the page's footer) once the JIT's cache was flushed: {{blocks}} compiled, {{flushes}} flushes.

statusbar.blocks.flushed.title.message: The JIT has compiled {{blocks}} blocks; its cache was flushed {{flushes}}×.
statusbar.blocks.flushed.title.note: Tooltip of the Blocks compiled element in the status bar (the page's footer) once the JIT's cache was flushed: {{blocks}} compiled since boot, {{flushes}} flushes.

statusbar.blocks.note: The Blocks compiled element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{blocks}} blocks the JIT compiled since boot.

statusbar.blocks.title.note: Tooltip of the Blocks compiled element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{blocks}} blocks the JIT compiled since boot.

statusbar.compile.note: The Compile time element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{time}} is the time spent compiling since boot, in seconds ("9.3 s").

statusbar.compile.title.message: The JIT has spent {{time}} compiling since boot.
statusbar.compile.title.note: Tooltip of the Compile time element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{time}} is the time spent compiling since boot, in seconds.

statusbar.jitcache.use.note: The JIT cache's use in the status bar (the page's footer) (its short value, and inside its words and tooltip): {{live}} the compiled code alive, {{budget}} the cache's budget (sizes).

statusbar.jitcache.note: The JIT cache element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{cache}} is its use ("61 MiB of 320 MiB").

statusbar.jitcache.title.note: Tooltip of the JIT cache element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{cache}} is its use ("61 MiB of 320 MiB").

statusbar.net.traffic.note: A network element's value in the status bar (the page's footer) (traffic: bytes a second; total: bytes since the start): {{rx}} received, {{tx}} sent, each a size or a rate ("1.4 MiB/s").

statusbar.net.all.note: The network traffic or total element for every adapter in the status bar (the page's footer) (its screen-reader text when drawn with arrows): {{traffic}} is received and sent.

statusbar.net.all.total.title.message: Bytes received and sent by every adapter since the machine started.
statusbar.net.all.total.title.note: Tooltip of the Network total element for every adapter in the status bar (the page's footer).

statusbar.net.all.rate.title.message: Bytes a second received and sent by every adapter.
statusbar.net.all.rate.title.note: Tooltip of the Network traffic element for every adapter in the status bar (the page's footer).

statusbar.net.all.label.note: The word before the received and sent arrows of the network element for every adapter in the status bar (the page's footer): short for network.

statusbar.net.one.note: A network traffic or total element for one adapter in the status bar (the page's footer) (its screen-reader text when drawn with arrows): {{name}} is the adapter's name, {{traffic}} received and sent.

statusbar.net.one.total.title.message: Bytes received and sent by {{name}} since the machine started.
statusbar.net.one.total.title.note: Tooltip of the Network total element for one adapter in the status bar (the page's footer): {{name}} is the adapter's name.

statusbar.net.one.rate.title.message: Bytes a second received and sent by {{name}}.
statusbar.net.one.rate.title.note: Tooltip of the Network traffic element for one adapter in the status bar (the page's footer): {{name}} is the adapter's name.

statusbar.disk.traffic.note: A disk element's value in the status bar (the page's footer) (speed: bytes a second; total: bytes since the start): R read {{read}}, W written {{written}}, each a size or a rate.

statusbar.disk.all.note: The Disk speed or Disk total element for every disk in the status bar (the page's footer): {{traffic}} is read (R) and written (W).

statusbar.disk.all.total.title.message: Bytes read (R) and written (W) on all disks since the machine started.
statusbar.disk.all.total.title.note: Tooltip of the Disk total element for every disk in the status bar (the page's footer).

statusbar.disk.all.rate.title.message: Bytes a second read (R) and written (W) on all disks.
statusbar.disk.all.rate.title.note: Tooltip of the Disk speed element for every disk in the status bar (the page's footer).

statusbar.disk.name.note: A disk's name in the status bar (the page's footer)'s disk elements when the page doesn't know its file's name: {{number}} counts from 1, as the machine's Disks tab lists them.

statusbar.disk.one.note: A Disk speed or Disk total element for one disk in the status bar (the page's footer): {{name}} is the disk's name (its file), {{traffic}} read (R) and written (W).

statusbar.disk.one.total.title.message: Bytes read (R) and written (W) on {{name}} since the machine started.
statusbar.disk.one.total.title.note: Tooltip of the Disk total element for one disk in the status bar (the page's footer): {{name}} is the disk's name.

statusbar.disk.one.rate.title.message: Bytes a second read (R) and written (W) on {{name}}.
statusbar.disk.one.rate.title.note: Tooltip of the Disk speed element for one disk in the status bar (the page's footer): {{name}} is the disk's name.

statusbar.usb.traffic.note: A USB element's value in the status bar (the page's footer) (traffic: bytes a second; total: bytes since the start): {{in}} what the USB devices gave the guest, {{out}} what they took from it, each a size or a rate ("1.4 MiB/s").

statusbar.usb.note: The USB traffic or total element in the status bar (the page's footer) (its screen-reader text when drawn with arrows): {{traffic}} is in and out.

statusbar.usb.label.note: The word before the in and out arrows of the USB element in the status bar (the page's footer).

statusbar.usb.rate.title.message: Bytes a second the USB devices gave the machine (in) and took from it (out), all of them together.
statusbar.usb.rate.title.note: Tooltip of the USB traffic element in the status bar (the page's footer).

statusbar.usb.total.title.message: Bytes the USB devices gave the machine (in) and took from it (out) since it started, all of them together.
statusbar.usb.total.title.note: Tooltip of the USB total element in the status bar (the page's footer).

statusbar.cpu.mips.note: The MIPS element in the status bar (the page's footer) (and per vCPU in its tooltip): {{value}} is millions of guest instructions run in the last second, or several vCPUs' values separated by spaces, or … before the first second.

statusbar.cpu.jit.note: The JIT share element in the status bar (the page's footer) (and per vCPU in its tooltip): {{value}} is the percentage of instructions run in compiled code ("98.7%"), or several vCPUs' separated by spaces.

statusbar.cpu.mips.title.note: Tooltip of the machine's MIPS element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{value}} is the millions of guest instructions run in the last second.

statusbar.cpu.jit.title.message: {{value}} of the instructions run as compiled code.
statusbar.cpu.jit.title.note: Tooltip of the machine's JIT share element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{value}} is a percentage ("98.7%").

statusbar.cpu.line.note: A line of the tooltip of a per-vCPU MIPS or JIT share element in the status bar (the page's footer): {{vcpu}} is the vCPU's number (from 0), {{value}} its value with its unit ("310 MIPS").

statusbar.cpu.one.note: A MIPS or JIT share element for one vCPU in the status bar (the page's footer): {{vcpu}} is its number (from 0), {{value}} its value with its unit ("310 MIPS").

statusbar.cpu.bars.mips.note: Screen-reader text of the MIPS element drawn as a bar per vCPU in the status bar (the page's footer) (the tooltip gives each vCPU's value).

statusbar.cpu.bars.jit.note: Screen-reader text of the JIT share element drawn as a bar per vCPU in the status bar (the page's footer) (the tooltip gives each vCPU's value).

statusbar.sample.net1.note: Made-up words for the Preferences' status bar editor's preview while no machine runs: the first sample adapter's connection (a tailnet named home) and its state, in a Connection element's tooltip.

statusbar.sample.net2.note: Made-up words for the Preferences' status bar editor's preview while no machine runs: the second sample adapter, with no connection, in a Connection element's tooltip.

StatusBar.link.note: After the adapter's name in the Connection element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer): {{connection}} is the connection's name, {{state}} how it's going (as the Network menu says it).

StatusBar.link.none.note: After the adapter's name in the Connection element's tooltip in the status bar (the page's footer), for an adapter with no connection: {{state}} is its state (Not connected).

StatusEditor.sample.state.note: The power state shown in the Preferences' status bar editor's preview while no machine runs (made-up numbers).

StatusEditor.look.text.note: Radio choice in the settings of a chosen element in the Preferences' status bar editor: the element shows in words.

StatusEditor.look.icon.note: Radio choice in the settings of a chosen element in the Preferences' status bar editor: the element shows as its icon and short value (its words in the tooltip).

StatusEditor.look.both.note: Radio choice in the settings of a chosen element in the Preferences' status bar editor: its icon and its words.

StatusEditor.device.cpu.note: Label of the number field (and screen-reader name of its group) in the Preferences' status bar editor for an element that shows one vCPU: which one.

StatusEditor.device.net.note: Label of the number field (and screen-reader name of its group) in the Preferences' status bar editor for an element that shows one network adapter: which one.

StatusEditor.device.disk.note: Label of the number field (and screen-reader name of its group) in the Preferences' status bar editor for an element that shows one disk: which one.

StatusEditor.index.cpu.message: Numbered from 0, as the guest names them (cpu0). Hidden on a machine that doesn't have it.
StatusEditor.index.cpu.note: Note beside the vCPU number field of a one-vCPU element in the Preferences' status bar editor.

StatusEditor.index.net.message: Numbered from 1, as the machine's Network tab lists them. Hidden on a machine that doesn't have it.
StatusEditor.index.net.note: Note beside the Adapter number field of a one-adapter element in the Preferences' status bar editor (the Network tab is the Machines page's).

StatusEditor.index.disk.message: Numbered from 1, as the machine's Disks tab lists them. Hidden on a machine that doesn't have it.
StatusEditor.index.disk.note: Note beside the Disk number field of a one-disk element in the Preferences' status bar editor (the Disks tab is the Machines page's).

StatusEditor.bar.note: Screen-reader name of the copy of the status bar in Preferences whose chips are the bar's elements, in order.

StatusEditor.chip.title.note: Tooltip of an element's chip in the Preferences' status bar editor, on three lines; a click chooses it. {{name}} is the element's name, {{about}} what it shows (a sentence).

StatusEditor.chip.title.absent.note: Tooltip of a dimmed element's chip in the Preferences' status bar editor, on three lines: the running machine hasn't its device (a second disk). {{name}} is the element's name, {{about}} what it shows (a sentence).

StatusEditor.spacer.note: The words on a spacer's chip in the Preferences' status bar editor (between arrows: it takes the free room).

StatusEditor.remove.title.note: Tooltip of the × on an element's chip in the Preferences' status bar editor.

StatusEditor.remove.label.note: Screen-reader name of the × on an element's chip in the Preferences' status bar editor. {{name}} is the element's name.

StatusEditor.empty.message: No elements, so no status bar is shown. Add some below.
StatusEditor.empty.note: Shown in the Preferences' status bar editor's bar when it has no element; the palette below adds them.

StatusEditor.sample.message: Showing made-up numbers. With a machine running, it shows the machine's own.
StatusEditor.sample.note: Note under the Preferences' status bar editor's bar while no machine runs: the chips show a made-up machine's numbers.

StatusEditor.running.note: Note under the Preferences' status bar editor's bar while a machine runs: the chips show its numbers.

StatusEditor.nothing.message: None of these elements shows anything, so no status bar is shown.
StatusEditor.nothing.note: Note under the Preferences' status bar editor's bar (after Showing…) when its elements are all spacers or dividers.

StatusEditor.defaults.note: Button under the Preferences' status bar editor's bar: puts back the elements a browser starts with.

StatusEditor.look.note: Screen-reader name of the group of look choices (Words, Icon, Icon and words) in the settings of a chosen element in the Preferences' status bar editor.

StatusEditor.cpus.note: Screen-reader name of the group of choices (Bars, Numbers) for an each-vCPU element in the Preferences' status bar editor.

StatusEditor.cpus.bars.note: Radio choice for an each-vCPU element in the Preferences' status bar editor: a bar per vCPU.

StatusEditor.cpus.numbers.note: Radio choice for an each-vCPU element in the Preferences' status bar editor: each vCPU's number.

StatusEditor.left.note: Tooltip of the left arrow button in the settings of a chosen element in the Preferences' status bar editor.

StatusEditor.right.note: Tooltip of the right arrow button in the settings of a chosen element in the Preferences' status bar editor.

StatusEditor.remove.note: Button (with a bin icon) in the settings of a chosen element in the Preferences' status bar editor: removes it from the bar.

StatusEditor.palette.note: Screen-reader name of the palette under the Preferences' status bar editor: the elements that can be added, by group.

StatusEditor.add.title.message:
{{about}}
Click to add it at the end, or drag it into the bar.
StatusEditor.add.title.note: Tooltip of an element's chip in the palette of the Preferences' status bar editor. {{about}} is what the element shows.

ui.loading.note: The power state at the left of the status bar (the page's footer) when the page opens, before the machine's first state.
